title: Private Deploy: Dynamic License Banding, Patch Window Credits, and Security Questionnaire Fastpath
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Run a product experiment to validate a dynamic licensing model for Private/VPC/on‑prem customers that pairs variable license bands with optional 'patch window credits' and a prioritized Security Questionnaire (SQ) fastpath. Goal: increase sales velocity for constrained procurement teams while preserving predictable ARR and limiting operational risk. Hypotheses: 1) Flexible bands priced by committed baseline RPS/GPU-hours reduce sales friction for mid‑market customers; 2) Bundled patch-window credits (emergency hotfix / expedited minor upgrades) reduce support escalations and license churn in the first 6 months; 3) a documented SQ fastpath and templated answers with SLA for turnaround (<10 business days) materially shortens contract cycles for regulated customers. Deliverables: pricing matrix, contract amendment templates, SQ fastpath playbook, telemetry/metrics to evaluate churn/uptake, and a pilot offer for 3 target accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing matrix with at least three dynamic bands defined (Baseline, Flex, FlexPlus) and ARRs per band
Patch-window credit SKU defined and billing/unit economics modeled (one-time vs recurring)
SQ fastpath runbook written with owner, SLAs, and template answers for top 12 SQ items
Legal/Finance sign-off on amendment language for band movement and prorations
Pilot offer ready and 3 sales-qualified customers identified for trial
Telemetry events and a dashboard to track uptake, churn, support escalations, and upgrade cadence
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with sales engineering, legal, and support. Agreed scope: bands will be defined by committed GPU-hour equivalent and optional overage buckets.
2026-03-01: Finance modeled three revenue scenarios; baseline shows neutral ARPU if uptake of patch-window credits >20%.
2026-03-05: Security provided initial feedback on SQ fastpath: they prefer a gated 'fastpath' for customers with an executed NDA & SOC2 attestation; added as constraint.
2026-03-10: Draft pricing matrix created; legal requested explicit language for upgrade / downgrade prorations and retention of support credits.
2026-03-12: Identified three pilot accounts (two mid-market, one enterprise) willing to trial a 6-month banded commitment with credits; sales assigned owners.
2026-03-14: Implementation spike scheduled with billing/engineering for telemetry events and a pilot promo code flow; estimate 2 sprints of eng work.
risks: Revenue dilution if customers move large workloads to lower bands without proportional commitments
Legal exposure on prorated upgrades/rollbacks leading to billing disputes
Operational load if patch-window credits are misused by pilot customers leading to increased on-call effort
Security team bandwidth for SQ fastpath may become a bottleneck if demand exceeds capacity
notes: Proposed mitigation: require minimum 3-month baseline commitment before eligibility for SQ fastpath and tiered fastpath SLAs based on support plan.
Consider a pilot-only cap on patch-window credit redemption to limit first-month operational exposure.
Align telemetry with Console team: track 'band_upgrade', 'band_downgrade', 'patch_credit_redeemed', and 'sq_fastpath_request' events.
Follow-up: sync with Dedicated product manager week of 2026-03-16 to align on capacity reservation language.
